html:
St Stephen's Cathedral, the Stephansdom, stands at the centre of Vienna. A church was begun here in 1137, and the present Gothic building, with its south tower of 136 metres, was raised from 1304 to the 1400s.

Its roof of coloured glazed tiles, laid in zigzags and with the double-headed eagle of the Habsburgs, is famous. The great bell, the Pummerin, was cast from cannon left by the Ottomans after the siege of 1683. Mozart was married here and his funeral was held in a chapel of the cathedral.

The roof burned in April 1945 in the last days of the Second World War, and its rebuilding was paid for by all of Austria's provinces, a sign of the new republic. The cathedral is the seat of the archbishop of Vienna and a symbol of Austria.
